_comment: GENERATED by Build/Scripts/build-grande-themes.mjs. The single source of truth for which themes exist.

themes.name: Neutral
themes.character: A pure grayscale spine. The accent is ink, not a colour, so nothing on the page competes with the content.
themes.use: Documentation, dashboards, anything where the interface should disappear.

themes.name: Butter
themes.character: Cream paper with one vivid blue. The only theme whose accent really shouts.
themes.use: Marketing pages and product launches that want a single confident colour.

themes.name: Chocolate
themes.character: Warm browns with a serif for headings — the only theme that mixes two type families of different species.
themes.use: Editorial writing, long reads, anything with a printed feel.

themes.name: Matcha
themes.character: Deep green on paper, headings set in a handwriting face, and the softest corners in the set.
themes.use: Craft, food, wellbeing — places where a human hand should show.

themes.name: Stone
themes.character: Cool grey with Montserrat headings over a Figtree body. Quiet and architectural.
themes.use: Corporate and professional-services sites that want restraint.

themes.name: Gothic
themes.character: Dark even in light mode — the one theme that does not flip. Near-white on near-black at every hour.

themes.name: Y2K
themes.character: Lavender canvas and square corners: radius zero, the only theme with no rounding at all.
themes.use: Playful, retro-leaning brands that want to look deliberately unsoftened.

themes.name: Harbour
themes.character: Deep maritime navy with a cool grey page. The most conservative of the set — the one to reach for when a site has to look institutional.

themes.name: Ember
themes.character: Warm charcoal lit by a single ember orange. Reads as evening rather than alarm, and keeps the orange for the one thing that matters on the page.

themes.name: Linen
themes.character: A soft warm neutral built for long-form reading: low contrast between paper and surface, generous type, nothing competing with the text.

themes.name: Orchid
themes.character: Muted purple with a cool paper. Distinctive without shouting, and the only theme in the set whose accent reads as decorative rather than corporate.

themes.name: Cobalt
themes.character: A saturated engineering blue on near-white. Built for dashboards and documentation, where a strong accent has to survive being repeated fifty times.

themes.name: Moss
themes.character: Deep forest green, quieter and colder than Astryx's own matcha. For organisations that want green without looking like a wellness brand.

themes.name: Clay
themes.character: Terracotta and warm stone. Earthy without being rustic, and the softest radius in the set so nothing has a hard corner.

themes.name: Plum
themes.character: Deep aubergine on a faintly warm page. Dark, adult and a little editorial — the theme for a publication rather than a product.

themes.name: Sand
themes.character: Desert warmth: pale ochre paper, dark umber ink. Bright without being white, which suits sites read outdoors or on cheap screens.

themes.name: Ink
themes.character: Near-black on white at the highest contrast the set offers. The one to pick when an accessibility statement has to survive scrutiny.

themes.name: Lagoon
themes.character: Blue-green water on pale sand. Fresher than Cobalt and warmer than Harbour, without tipping into turquoise.

themes.name: Rose
themes.character: Dusty rose, deliberately desaturated so it reads as considered rather than sweet. Pairs a serif heading with a plain body.

themes.name: Graphite
themes.character: Cool monochrome with no hue at all in the brand colours. The neutral of last resort, for sites whose imagery has to supply every bit of colour.

themes.name: Frost
themes.character: Arctic blue-grey, desaturated to the point of calm. Adapted from the Nord palette (MIT); the coldest theme in the set and the one that stays legible under bright office light.

themes.name: Latte
themes.character: Pastel mauve on a cool white page. Adapted from Catppuccin Latte (MIT) — softer than Orchid and the friendliest theme here, for products that would rather be liked than admired.

themes.name: Solar
themes.character: Cream paper and dark cyan, on the CIELAB-balanced relationships Ethan Schoonover published as Solarized (MIT). Low contrast by design, for interfaces read for hours rather than glanced at.

themes.name: Retro
themes.character: Warm amber on aged cream, adapted from Gruvbox (MIT). The only theme whose paper is properly yellow rather than merely off-white, and the one that reads as a printed manual.

themes.name: Midnight
themes.character: Indigo on a faintly blue page, adapted from Tokyo Night (MIT). Built dark-first upstream, so it is the theme whose dark mode looks intentional rather than inverted.
